coverage: Pier & Point covers four sites on San Francisco's central waterfront: Mission Rock, Mission Bay, Pier 70 and Potrero Power Station. A parcel that is not in this data is outside coverage, not "no activity".

record.name: Pier 70 Parcel E4
record.summary: The waterfront arts-building parcel east of Building 21: excluded from the developer's purchase option, capped at 50 ft and five stories, and reserved under the 2017 DDA for a roughly 90,000 sq ft arts facility (with replacement studios for the Noonan Building artists) on a 50-year, $1-a-year lease once $17.5 million in private contributions is raised. The Port's proposed 2026 amendments would rezone it to allow housing if the arts facility proves infeasible.

notes.accuracy_caveat: APPROXIMATE -- this block is not yet built and does not correspond to any subdivided Assessor parcel: it currently sits on vacant/graded land, surface parking, or an existing industrial building slated for demolition within Brookfield's 28-acre district (unaddressed in DataSF's Assessor roll). Redone 2026-09-14 with a corrected, shear-free transform (see digitization_method) -- treat vertex positions as accurate to roughly 5-15m, not survey-grade. NOTE: this polygon is NOT clipped against real streets or existing buildings -- unlike Potrero's approximate blocks, several of Pier 70's D4D blocks are sited on existing industrial buildings that will be demolished, so overlap with a currently-real building is often expected, not an error; a boundary that appears to touch or slightly cross a street centerline reflects this transform's 1-8m residual error, not a deliberate encroachment.
notes.digitized_from: Pier 70 Design for Development, Figure 6.4.2 - Maximum Building Height (p.155).
notes.why_no_real_parcel: A real Assessor parcel may exist under this block (part of Brookfield's larger, largely unaddressed 28-acre site), but it has not been subdivided per the masterplan's individual named parcels -- this uses hand-traced approximate geometry instead.
notes.regulatory_context: Designated use is 'Arts' per both the D4D (excluded from the developer's standard parcel-purchase option as 'the arts building parcel') and Brookfield's own leasing brochure -- NOT residential or general mixed-use as sometimes described secondhand. Recorded here as 'mixed' only because this map has no dedicated 'arts' use category; treat the real designation as Arts. Max height 50 ft per Figure 6.4.2 -- the lowest of any parcel at Pier 70. No construction-start source found.

facts.value: FC Pier 70, LLC, an affiliate of Brookfield Properties (originally Forest City)
Port of San Francisco (Seawall Lot 349; option parcels are ground-leased for 99 years except condominium parcels, which may be sold)
SITELAB urban studio (lead author); Grimshaw Architecture (commercial), David Baker Architects (residential), James Corner Field Operations (landscape)
Arts (the D4D permits office uses in E4 except on the ground floor; Priority Retail required on at least 33% of its east and south frontages, S2.2.3)
50 (D4D Figure 6.4.2), the lowest of any new parcel
90,000 sq ft arts facility with replacement studio space (Port project page); 'waterfront arts facility' in the 2018 groundbreaking release
50 years at $1/year base rent with a 15-year extension option, per the 2017 DDA major terms (the memo's mark-up also shows '66 year lease')
Excluded from the developer's option under the DDA, with the affordable parcels, C1A and historic Buildings 12 and 21
Phase 2C with E1 and Building 21 (Port's proposed 2026 phasing plan, Exhibit A)
Permanent replacement space for the Noonan Building artists 'will likely be located on the site of Parcel E4', at restricted rents tied to the Port's parameter rent (then $1.30/gsf)

open_questions: No arts operator, fundraising progress toward the $17.5 million, or design for the Arts Building was found; the DDA ties its start to three years after completion of the office building on Parcel 'B-2'.
SF YIMBY's 2021 summary attributes ~115,000 gsf of retail and arts space to Building 21 and ~120,000 gsf to 'E-1A and E-1B', with no separate arts building; the underlying filing was not retrieved.
Whether the Noonan Building has been demolished or its tenants relocated to temporary space: the June 2025 Port deck still lists 'Noonan Open Studios' and the Noonan Artists as active on site.
